title: Trump: US expanding defense cooperation with the Philippines
summary: United States President Donald Trump on Wednesday said America is expanding its defense cooperation with the Philippines amid its continuing moves to sell US weapons to its treaty partner in…

blocks.text: United States President Donald Trump on Wednesday said America is expanding its defense cooperation with the Philippines amid its continuing moves to sell US weapons to its treaty partner in Southeast Asia.
Trump spoke on the matter as he and Philippine President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. held bilateral talks during the US president's state visit to the Philippines.
"Working with President Marcos, we're also expanding our defense cooperation, which has always been a key pillar of security for this part of the world," Trump said during his speech.
The US president also said that since he took office, he has approved arms sales to the Philippines of over $5 billion.
Trump also shared that the US is expanding its armaments factory with the construction of some 21 plants.
Asked about maritime tensions in the West Philippine Sea, Trump said, "I'm not concerned about that at all. That'll be taken care of."

Trump's response was also in line with a question asking about the United States' preparedness with regard to its Mutual Defense Treaty (MDT) with the Philippines. The MDT, signed in 1951, commits the Philippines and the United States to come to each other's defense in the event of an armed attack on either country.

Trump's presence in the Philippines from November 17 to 18 has drawn protests from various groups, condemning his alleged role in soaring fuel prices due to the US-Israel war with Iran, as well as the US-led Pax Silica initiative. — VDV, GMA News
